objective: Standard statement: (1) a crossing site whose wire A runs from its point end and wire B from its line end, with a start rung and rungs between junctions (no caps), acts exactly by (NW)^k, where W is the junction and N the rung, so the exact crossing is the identity (the k = 0 term); (2) for the junction of two plain cubes, S' = NW has eigenvalues (19 +- sqrt 365)/2 and (-7 +- i sqrt 3)/2, a unit of norm -1 in Q(sqrt 365) and the two primes above 13 in Z[omega], so the squared products are distinct for distinct count vectors of equal total (lattice condition); (3) demonstration: #col(K3,3) = 6 recovered from plain instances with 1, 3, 5, 7 junctions, each plain, cubic bipartite, certified Pfaffian, a brace, and twisted on all three branches at every junction; (4) observation: all 2500 plain ladder steps are nonsingular and two generic ones generate the full parity-block algebra. Controls: the unreversed site (as in SOFT-CROSS A, cap replaced by a rung) does not span the exact crossing with one junction type; one count alone is not the answer. Nearest known result: interpolation of crossovers (Valiant; Cai, Lu, Xia); none for braces found.
status: Proved: ladders of plain cube junctions interpolate to an exact crossing inside braces; the reversed site acts by (NW)^k with characteristic polynomial (x^2 - 19x - 1)(x^2 + 7x + 13) (a unit of Q(sqrt 365), Eisenstein primes above 13: lattice condition); #col(K3,3) = 6 from plain Pfaffian braces of 20 to 104 vertices.
title: A plain crossing inside braces
